facts.text: First settled in 1805 by Alexander Moffatt, Limerick grew around a mill owned by Samuel Shelley and became a post office and railroad station by the late 19th century.
The community’s early growth was spurred by the expansion of Fort Drum, a U.S. Army installation that reshaped the local economy in the late 20th century.
Limerick’s settlers arrived after the Revolutionary War, part of a wave that opened northern New York lands through treaties with Indigenous nations.
In the early 1800s, John Baxter, Abner Smith, and Isaac Moffatt removed a reef of rocks at the Perch River rapids to drain flooded flats and improve land use for the growing community.
Limerick’s name echoes the Irish city, a nod to the settlers’ heritage, though the town itself never reached the size of its namesake.
